to.implementation_strategy: Extend the existing change/governance stack rather than building new tooling. Reuse core/change_registry.py and core/change_spec.py as the model of 'a change'; add a classifier that assigns each change a kind + sensitivity + shipping flag; enforce the language rule ('shipped+sensitive -> Go') from BI-PF-0387/0388; add a dependency scanner that reads declared manifests (go.mod, requirements/pyproject) and fails CI when a runtime import is undeclared. Wire enforcement into core/guardrails.py and core/run_guard.py and expose kinds via the existing /api/v1/changes/kinds endpoint. Persist classifier policy in config/guardrail-policy.json (extend, not replace).

dependency_findings.required_state: policy settled: shipped+sensitive -> Go rule defined
ADR accepted: compiled-only shipping, one source many editions
in_progress — EPIC A includes A6
planned — A6 language rule only becomes enforceable once the Go home exists

conflict_findings: core/guardrails.py and core/run_guard.py are shared surfaces likely touched by BI-0219 (output guardrails) and BI-PF-0418 (parallel run engine); serialize merges or isolate new rules behind config-driven policy entries.
/api/v1/changes endpoints are also consumed by BI-PF-0432 tooling; adding kinds must be backward compatible.
config/guardrail-policy.json is a hot config file; coordinate edits to avoid schema churn conflicts.
duplication_findings: core/agent_rules.py already encodes rule enforcement — extend it for the language rule instead of a new rules engine.
core/change_log.py + core/change_registry.py already track change kinds — the classifier should populate these, not create a parallel registry.
BI-0218 (evals/versioning) and BI-PF-0418 (parallel run engine) also touch run-time guards; ensure drift guard is additive to core/run_guard.py, not a fork.
BI-PF-0432 (dedup marking) is process-level, not code-level; no overlap beyond grooming conventions.
to.rationale: Reuse-first: the change registry, guardrails, and rule modules already exist and form the natural substrate for a classifier and two new enforcement rules. No new component is needed; the work is EXTEND of existing governance surfaces plus config and CI wiring. The item governs A1-A7 so it must land early but after BI-PF-0394 provides the Go target for the language rule.
assumptions: Every change already registers in core/change_registry.py with a kind; if not, the classifier becomes the registrar.
Runtime dependency declarations live in standard manifests (go.mod, pyproject.toml/requirements.txt).
The language rule can be approximated by path/sensitivity tags (e.g., 'shipped' and 'sensitive' labels on change specs) rather than static analysis of code content.
CI can run the classifier + scanners as a pre-merge gate.
risks: Classifier false positives (marking a change shipped+sensitive when it is not) could block CI — mitigate with an override/adjudication path recorded in the change registry.
Dependency scanner may produce noise for optional/dev imports — mitigate by scoping to runtime deps only and whitelisting declared extras.
Language rule enforcement depends on BI-PF-0394's Go home existing; until then, the rule can only warn, not fail.
Policy config schema changes may break older runners — version the policy format.

The item governs A1-A7 so it must land early but after BI-PF-0394 provides the Go target for the language rule.
assumptions: Every change already registers in core/change_registry.py with a kind; if not, the classifier becomes the registrar.
Runtime dependency declarations live in standard manifests (go.mod, pyproject.toml/requirements.txt).
The language rule can be approximated by path/sensitivity tags (e.g., 'shipped' and 'sensitive' labels on change specs) rather than static analysis of code content.
CI can run the classifier + scanners as a pre-merge gate.
risks: Classifier false positives (marking a change shipped+sensitive when it is not) could block CI — mitigate with an override/adjudication path recorded in the change registry.
Dependency scanner may produce noise for optional/dev imports — mitigate by scoping to runtime deps only and whitelisting declared extras.
Language rule enforcement depends on BI-PF-0394's Go home existing; until then, the rule can only warn, not fail.
Policy config schema changes may break older runners — version the policy format.
evidence: candidate components: core/agent_rules.py, core/change_log.py, core/change_registry.py, core/change_spec.py, core/guardrails.py, core/run_guard.py
related: BI-PF-0387 (language rule source policy, score 0.20)
related: BI-PF-0429 (guard rules in AGENTS.md precedents, score 0.14)

Override/adjudication workflow for classifier decisions.
Which dependency ecosystems the no-undeclared-dep check covers (Go modules, Python, both).
